% torsion_sources.tex — per-group dated source lists for rational torsion on
% genus-2 Jacobians /Q, each reference classified (protocol of 2026-07-21).
% Generated by code/claude_gen_torsion_sources.py.
\documentclass[10pt]{amsart}
\usepackage{longtable}
\usepackage[margin=1.8cm]{geometry}
\usepackage[colorlinks=true,linkcolor=blue,citecolor=blue,urlcolor=blue]{hyperref}
\title{Sources for rational torsion subgroups on genus-2 Jacobians over $\mathbb{Q}$:\\
dated and classified}
\date{July 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\noindent For each torsion subgroup we list, in date order, the located sources
that construct or exhibit it.  \emph{Inclusion rule:} the list aims to be
exhaustive for explicit pre-2016 constructions and for proven geometrically
simple realizations, and is representative (not exhaustive) for split
constructions and for post-2016 database rows.  A group has a section here only
if it has some located literature beyond the databases; groups whose only
witnesses are the production LMFDB, the extended Booker--Sutherland database, or
the present paper (e.g.\ $[63]$, $[35]$, $[45]$, $[60]$, $[2,24]$, $[3,12]$
appearing inside the notes below) are not given their own section.

\emph{Classification.} \textbf{geom.\ simple} = the source proves geometric
(absolute) simplicity, or the displayed curve is independently certified so;
\textbf{$\mathbb{Q}$-simple only}; \textbf{split} = explicitly split
construction; \textbf{mixed} = a database or family row containing both
geometrically simple and non-simple curves; \textbf{claimed} = simplicity
asserted without proof; \textbf{not addressed}; \textbf{context} = a related
result that is \emph{not} itself a realization of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational torsion
on a genus-2 Jacobian (a lead over a larger field, a torsion-free or Galois-stable-only
example, an isogeny kernel, or a Prym rather than a Jacobian), retained for
lineage.  A $*$ marks a classification not verified against the original text
(taken instead from a review, survey, or citing paper).
\medskip

\subsection*{$[5]$}
\begin{longtable}{p{0.9cm} p{7.6cm} p{2.3cm} p{4.2cm}}
\hline Year & Construction & Class & Reference / note \\ \hline
1961* & $w^5{=}u(1{-}u)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_5)$: rank 0 (a lead over $\mathbb{Q}(\mu_5)$, not over $\mathbb{Q}$) & context & \cite{Faddeev1961}\\
1973* & $J_0(31)$: cuspidal class of order 5 (exact by Mazur 1977) & not addressed & \cite{Ogg1973} (RM, geom.\ simple (LMFDB 961.a))\\
1978* & Fermat-quotient cusp classes over $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)$ & context & \cite{GrossRohrlich1978}\\
1986 & full torsion packet of $y^2{-}y{=}x^5$, explicit & not addressed & \cite{Coleman1986} (end of paper; the source cited by Boxall--Grant (0.2))\\
1991 & 2-param family, exact order 5 (Result 1, $g{=}2$) & not addressed & \cite{Flynn1991}\\
2000 & torsion packet of $y^2{-}y{=}x^5$; $J$ CM by $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_5]$ & geom.\ simple & \cite{BoxallGrant2000} (\S5: absolutely simple (CM curve))\\
2001 & universal 3-param family with marked 5-torsion & not addressed & \cite{BGL2001} (word simple absent from the paper)\\
2004 & two 2-param 5-families (one contains $X_0(31)$) & geom.\ simple & \cite{LPS2004} (generically absolutely irreducible)\\
2016 & 725 exact-$[5]$: 650 geom.\ simple, rest RM/CM/split & mixed & \cite{BSSVY} (DB)\\
\hline\end{longtable}
